reason: Start the vessel route with an artery by lining its pressure-resistant wall.

reason: Line the capillary support sleeves to build the vessels where exchange can occur.
expectation: I expect a thin endothelial capillary network supported by the sleeves, ready to connect to the artery.

reason: The only offered combination builds the venous vessel needed for the return route.

reason: Add valve folds to the veins; this is the only offered combination.

effect: The veins now have valves, and the illustration shows how limb-muscle compression helps move blood toward the heart.
reaction: The muscle-and-valve mechanism makes venous return more concrete.
reason: Join the exchange bed to venous return to complete the tissue route; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a connected route from arteries through capillaries to veins.

effect: The arterial, capillary and venous components now form a connected systemic route, completing the chapter goal.
reaction: The finished network is a clear summary, although its picture description is brief.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding venous valves was most worthwhile: the planned picture connects muscle compression and valve action to blood returning toward the heart.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the thin-walled veins was straightforward, but its picture description added little beyond the item name.

surprise.text: The venous-return picture showed how contracting limb muscles work alongside valves, rather than presenting the valves in isolation.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the capillary support sleeves and pericytes were not explained in the resulting brief capillary-bed description.

continue.text: I would consider continuing: connecting vessel structure to function was useful, especially the muscle-and-valve mechanism, though several assembly steps were predictable.
